questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose UCC primarily based on the courses I could choose as well as the student life. I liked that UCC has so many clubs and societies and the student life seemed very active.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The student office was very helpfull, but a bit slow. But I figured out everything I needed to know.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had arranged transfer from the airport, tours of the campus and a fair to join the clubs and societies.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was slightly difficult. You have to do it quite early to get something nice, and everything is very expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived off campus, but right next to it at a student accommodation (Brookfield Village). They were quite strict about visitors and parties. But it was really nice to live right next to campus. The rooms were very damp and got a bit moldy though..

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration was very stressfull. I was rejected from a lot of courses and needed to apply for new ones. I didn't know which courses I was actually going to take in the first weeks of the semester, and they told us to just go the classes and hope to be accepted. I ended up with good courses, but the process of getting there was very stresfull. I think is was worse because of the reduced capacity due to Covid.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You apply for courses before arriving and wait for approval. You have to make your own time table and make sure that none of your courses are overlapping. If you do not get the approval you need to register again and hope to be accepted for the new courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Student Office was very helpfull.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was rejected for a lot of courses because of the reduced capacity, but I ended up getting courses I wanted. I had to write the professors for a few courses to prove that I was qualified to take their courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to have a few extra courses to apply for, if you get rejected. And know that you might have to reach out the the professors.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was generally high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was only lectures and laboratory work, so you are a lot more independent. The syllabus is not a clear so you have to find literature on your own sometimes. But most professors were really helpfull, if you didn't understand something. They have a lo of "continuous assessment", so you have to be prepared to do a lot of tests all the time.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
"Introduction to Neuroscience, the Brain and Behaviour"
"Advanced Inorganic Chemistry Part 1"
"Advanced Analytical Chemistry Part 1"
"Western Music, Culture and Media"
"Structural and Experimental Biochemistry"
"Advanced Research Methodology in Neuroscience"

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
"Advanced Analytical Chemistry Part 1" was really interesting and fun. They focused a lot on the application and gave a lot of useful tips on careers.
"Advanced Research Methodology in Neuroscience" gave a lot of knowledge on conducting an experiment and how to work as a researcher.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My phone bill was very expensive the last month, because my phone company (3) raised the prices after being abroad for over 2 months.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transportation is not too expensive. Also restaurants are a lot cheaper than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of clubs and societies to join. There is a huge selection, so everyone can find something they like.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Taking trips around Ireland, hiking.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely hike. The mountaineering club has some nice trips, but you can easily plan them your self as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The Irish are so friendly, so it was very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open, and go out

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In Ireland they party during the week and go home on weekends. Otherwise it's not too different.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
There is a lot of test, so definitely keep up with studying all the time.
Take trips and see the country, it's so beautiful.
Join clubs and societies, there are so many and they do fun events all the time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to all the lectures and do extra reading. There is so much help to find, if things are difficult.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and learning to study in a diffrent way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing having fun and exploring a new city with studying. You want to have fun all the time, because there is so much to do, but sometimes you need to spend the weekend at the library.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
